front_blocks.md: Describe the bonding arrangement of carbon atoms in diamond.

back_blocks.md: In diamond, each carbon atom forms **covalent bonds** with four other carbon atoms in a **tetrahedral** arrangement. All electrons are held in covalent bonds, leaving **no free electrons**.

front_blocks.md: Diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon, meaning they contain only carbon atoms but have different structures.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Diamond and graphite are both **allotropes** of carbon: they both consist only of carbon atoms, but their different bonding arrangements give them completely different physical properties.

front_blocks.md: In graphite, each carbon atom bonds to **..........** others, leaving **..........** delocalised electron per atom, which allows graphite to **..........** electricity.

back_blocks.md: In graphite, each carbon atom bonds to **3** others, leaving **1** delocalised electron per atom, which allows graphite to **conduct** electricity.

cards.front_md: In graphite, each carbon atom bonds to **..........** others, leaving **..........** delocalised electron per atom, which allows graphite to **..........** electricity.
cards.back_md: In graphite, each carbon atom bonds to **3** others, leaving **1** delocalised electron per atom, which allows graphite to **conduct** electricity.

front_blocks.md: Why does diamond not conduct electricity but graphite does?

back_blocks.md: In diamond, all four outer electrons of each carbon atom are used in covalent bonds, leaving **no free electrons** to carry a charge.
In graphite, each carbon uses only three electrons for bonding, leaving one **delocalised electron** per atom that can move through the structure and carry a charge.

front_blocks.md: Graphite is slippery because the covalent bonds between carbon atoms within each layer are weak.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

The covalent bonds within each graphite layer are **strong**. Graphite is slippery because the forces between the layers are **weak intermolecular forces**, allowing the layers to slide over each other easily.

front_blocks.md: Why do both diamond and graphite have very high melting points?

back_blocks.md: Both diamond and graphite have **giant covalent structures**. A very large amount of energy is needed to break the many **strong covalent bonds** between carbon atoms throughout the structure, giving both substances very high melting points.

back_blocks.md: An **allotrope** is one of two or more different physical forms of the same element, in which the atoms are arranged in different structural patterns.
Diamond and graphite are both allotropes of carbon.

back_blocks.md: A metallic bond is the strong **electrostatic force** of attraction between a lattice of **positive metal ions** and the surrounding **delocalised electrons**. The delocalised electrons are free to move between the ions throughout the structure.

front_blocks.md: In a metal, atoms lose their outer electrons to become positive ions, while those electrons become delocalised and move freely through the lattice.

back_blocks.md: **True.**

Metal atoms lose their outer electrons to become **positive ions**. These electrons are no longer associated with any particular atom and are **delocalised**, forming a sea of electrons that holds the lattice together.

front_blocks.md: Why do metals have high melting points?

back_blocks.md: Metals have a giant structure with **strong electrostatic forces** of attraction between the positive metal ions and the **delocalised electrons** throughout the lattice. A large amount of energy is needed to overcome these forces.

front_blocks.md: Metals are malleable because the layers of positive ions can slide over each other without breaking the metallic bonds.

back_blocks.md: **True.**

The layers of **positive ions** in a metal can slide over each other when a force is applied. The **delocalised electrons** move to maintain the attraction throughout the structure, so the metal can be reshaped without shattering.

front_blocks.md: Why do metals conduct electricity but ionic compounds only conduct when molten or in solution?

back_blocks.md: Metals conduct electricity because **delocalised electrons** can move freely through the metal lattice at all times.
Ionic compounds can only conduct when molten or dissolved because in the solid state the **ions are in fixed positions** and cannot move to carry a charge.
